id: title:Gilbert09:say whether an azure scope or a role is wrong

review.posthog_relevance: Azure Cost Management connector credential and configuration validation, specifically distinguishing between malformed ARM paths and permission errors.
review.reason: The change adds input validation and status-dependent error handling to the Azure Cost Management connector. P1.F1.H1 adds a check to ensure the Azure Cost Management scope follows the expected ARM path format, preventing malformed inputs. P1.F1.H2 and P1.F1.H3 implement a helper and its integration to distinguish between 403 (permission denied) and 400/404 (not found) responses, a
review.uncertainty: The tier is assigned based on the implementation of bounded, substantive improvements to connector reliability and diagnostic quality. The tier does not account for unverified outcomes such as actual incident avoidance, adoption, or support ticket reduction, which remain unobserved. No tier assignment requested.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, complete change group. No unrelated PRs detected. No tier assignment requested.

observations.behavior: Adds a ValueError check requiring Azure Cost Management scope to contain a '/' and raises an error if not, alongside existing stripping and empty checks.
observations.code_quote: raise ValueError("Azure Cost Management scope must be an ARM path such as subscriptions/<subscription id>")
observations.posthog_connection: This prevents malformed or bare subscription IDs from proceeding to credential validation, potentially avoiding downstream 404s or ambiguous errors when the backend attempts to query Azure Cost Management dimensions.

observations.behavior: Adds a helper function to distinguish between 403 (permission denied) and 400/404 (not found) errors, returning specific remediation messages.
observations.posthog_connection: This improves the diagnostic quality of credential validation failures. Instead of a generic message, users receive specific instructions: either assign the 'Cost Management Reader' role or check the ARM path, depending on the HTTP status. This reduces support overhead and helps users self-correct configuration errors.

observations.behavior: Updates credential validation to call the new helper function, passing the caught exception, rather than returning a generic string.
observations.code_quote: "Could not read Azure Cost Management for that scope. Check the scope path and that the service principal has the Cost Management Reader role on it.",
observations.posthog_connection: This connects the new helper to the credential validation flow, replacing a generic error with a status-dependent, actionable message. This demonstrates the implementation of the improved diagnostics rather than just the helper's existence.
